newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - ADRs sag on rate hike fears.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - ADRs sag on rate hike fears.

text.p: Foreign companies' American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) sagged on Thursday amid fears that the U.S. Federal Reserve would raise interest rates.
Decliners led advancers 293 to 120 in mid-morning among 806 ADRS. The index of ADRs declined 0.65 percent and volume was 24 million shares.
Traders said ADRs were hit by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's hints that he was moving toward raising interest rates, perhaps as early as next week.
"The language is similar to the language that he used in January 1994 and in a week he raised rates," said Val Kosmider, head of international equity trading at Schroder Wertheim.
The Fed at that time raised its federal funds rate 25 basis points, the start of a series of rate-tightening moves.
Kosmider said there were few European shares standing out in morning trade, adding, "You kind of have to look at the macroeconomic situation."
British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc eased 1/8 to 59-5/8 in heavy volume dominated by a 1.3 million share block trade. Details on the block trade were not immediately available.
British Steel Plc rose 1/8 to 25-7/8 after it announced it would lay off "significantly more" than 5,000 jobs over the next five years.
The company also has been boosted by prospects for a shakeup in the European steel industry with a bid by Germany's Krupp for Thyssen AG vorm August Thyssen-Huette.
Latin American shares also eased, being especially sensitive to U.S. rate changes. Telefonos de Mexico, which closed at a 12-month high on Wednesday, fell 3/8 to 41-1/4 in heavy trade.
"When bonds fell, everything fell out of bed," a trader said, referring to a drop in U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds following Greenspan's remarks.
"Even magical Mexico is falling. This is driving everything," he said, referring to Greenspan.
